blocks.text:
Breakfast at the hotel.

Today you head to the tropical forest of **Mindo**.

The route follows the Pan-American Highway north, passing the Mitad del Mundo monument once again.

On the way, stop at a viewpoint overlooking the extinct **Pululahua** volcano. It offers views of the crater, described as the largest in Ecuador.

After the highest point of the route, the road descends towards Mindo. Highland scenery gradually gives way to lush tropical vegetation.

In Mindo, visit a **butterfly farm**, where you can see different species and observe stages of their development.

The area is also home to many hummingbirds.

Continue with a walk through the cloud forest. Hawks may be seen overhead, while woodpeckers can be heard among the trees.

Mindo is also home to partridges, American kestrels, guans, hummingbirds, cocks-of-the-rock and buntings.

The plant life is equally varied, with cedars, avocado trees, white, yellow and black cinnamon trees, red myrtle, cecropia, coriaria and nettles.

Next comes a **canopy ride above the forest**.

Travel over the treetops in a cable-car cabin, approximately **30 metres above the ground**. Safety equipment is used for the activity.

After the canopy ride, continue your walk through the tropical forest.

Another stop is a garden of **orchids**. More than **4,200 orchid species** grow in Ecuador, and the flower is considered one of the country's symbols.

After lunch, discover how chocolate is made at a small family-run chocolate factory.

Return to Quito in the evening.

Free evening.

Accommodation at **Mercure 4***. Breakfast included.

blocks.text:
Breakfast at the hotel.

Today you travel to **Quilotoa Crater Lake**.

From Quito, follow the Pan-American Highway towards the Cotopaxi Valley.

The first stop is a **rose plantation**. Flowers of many sizes and colours are grown here for export around the world.

During the visit, see how the roses are cut, selected and packed.

**Please note:** the plantation is not visited on weekends or public holidays.

Continue towards Quilotoa.

On the way, visit an artisan workshop in the village of **Tigua**, the birthplace of a local style of naïve painting in which Andean landscapes are painted on sheepskin.

After Tigua, the road heads towards the Central Andes along the **Pujilí Route**, passing through the village of Quilotoa.

On arrival, walk to the viewpoint overlooking the crater lake.

From here, you can see the water inside the volcanic crater and the surrounding mountain slopes.

The programme includes a walk through the local Indigenous community.

If you wish, and time permits, you can walk down to the lakeshore.

You can go **kayaking** on the lake and ride **mules** back up.

Kayaking and mule rides are **not included in the price**.

On the return journey to Quito, visit an Indigenous family in the Andean highlands to learn about local everyday life.

Return to Quito after the tour.

Accommodation at **Mercure 4***. Breakfast included.
